worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{3}-x}{{x}^{2}-3} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(x-\frac{1}{x})}{(1-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{x-0}{1-0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }x \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
